newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Key parties oppose Australian budget bill.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Key parties oppose Australian budget bill.

text.p: The Australian Labor and Democrat parties, which can almost block government legislation in the upper house of parliament, issued a joint condemnation of a budget measure on Tuesday.
The Liberal-National government wants to count retirement savings ("superannuation") in social security means tests for people aged between 55 and retirement age, thereby excluding some claimants.
But Labor and the Democrats recommended in a report on the government's bill that the measure be watered down, in part by ignoring the first A$250,000 of superannuation assets.
The bill is supposed to save A$93 million in the fiscal year to June 1998, its first full year of operation, and A$65 million in 1999/00.
No estimate of the cost of the amendments was available.
The bill is part of the government's deficit-slashing August budget, which aimed to save A$7.2 billion in 1997/98.
The government needs two extra votes to get a bill through the upper house, the Senate. Those votes can come from Labor, the Democrats, two Greens or two Independents.
